bullets.title: JPM shifts Tactically Bullish; NFP print today is the key catalyst
bullets.body: JPM turned Tactically Bullish on stabilizing yields, stronger growth PMIs, and tech earnings momentum. Feroli expects September NFP at 100k, unemployment 4.1%, AHE +0.2% m/m — a weak print viewed as bullish for bonds and yield-sensitive assets. Per sell-side survey, 80-120k payrolls and/or 4.1% urate is risk-on; only 6% of respondents expect a risk-off reaction.

bullets.title: Fed governors signal 2-3 total hikes vs. 4-5 priced by market; October hike off the table
bullets.body: Vice Chair Jefferson, NY Fed's Williams, and Governor Bowman all pushed back against an October rate hike. Multiple sources confirm Fed is guiding 2-3 total hikes while markets are pricing 4-5; Piper Sandler pegs 50bps additional hiking by early 2027 (likely March). 1y1y OIS fell 13bp to 4.78% on the dovish repricing.

bullets.title: 10Y yields at 2002 highs; bond volatility rising toward April 2025 stress levels
bullets.body: 10-year Treasury yields hit their highest level since 2002 after a sharp selloff, with JPM forecasting 5.20% near-term declining to 5.05% by year-end. The MOVE index has risen sharply toward April 2025 stress levels while corporate bond spreads widened the most since March amid record issuance. Treasury short positions are surging, raising repo borrowing costs and funding market disruption risks.

bullets.title: SPX futures +0.4-0.5% pre-market; AI and tech leading; October opens as tactical relief rally
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures +0.42-0.48% with NDX +0.74%; all Mag7 higher pre-market with semiconductors broadly up 1.8-2.4%. Piper characterizes October's open as a tactical relief rally, not a confirmed trend reversal, with AI and Energy remaining primary leadership groups. VIX staying below 19, remaining in the 'investable bucket.'

bullets.title: Eurozone inflation surged to 3-year high at 3.8%; ECB path complicated by energy shock
bullets.body: Euro area September HICP jumped to 3.76% y/y (vs consensus 3.6%), driven by energy prices surging 18.8% y/y after fuel gained 6.4% m/m. Core rose to 2.49%. JPM forecasts headline peaks at 3.9% by year-end before base effects drag it lower in 2027, assuming Brent declines to $90 by year-end (currently ~$100). Germany and Spain implemented fuel tax cuts partially offsetting the shock.

bullets.title: Oil mixed: WTI down ~3.4% on SPR release discussions, Brent still near $100 on geopolitical risk
bullets.body: WTI crude fell to $89.74 (-3.37%) as France/IEA discussed strategic reserve releases to cap diesel prices, while Brent traded near $99-102 with Ukraine attacks on Russian refineries keeping a geopolitical premium. Barclays raised its 4Q26 Brent forecast to $115 from $95. Jefferies flags MOVE index parallels and Brent above $100 as a signal the security environment remains fragile.

bullets.title: French fiscal crisis risk building; France-Germany 10Y spread >130bp, ECB unlikely to act before 250-300bp
bullets.body: France's 2027 budget targets a 5% deficit — well above the EU's 3% limit — in a parliament unlikely to pass sustainable fiscal policy. The France-Germany 10Y spread exceeds 130bp, highest since the euro area crisis. ECB's Transmission Protection Instrument is inapplicable to homemade fiscal problems; intervention is unlikely before spreads reach 250-300bp and would require ESM assistance or an emergency crisis budget.

bullets.title: Midterm prediction markets now price Democratic sweep at 60%; investors still positioned for gridlock
bullets.body: Jefferies notes prediction markets now assign 60% odds to a Democratic sweep of House and Senate, versus only 9% of investors expecting that outcome in August. Key Senate races are in data-center states (Texas, Ohio, Georgia) where AI infrastructure became a local election issue. A sweep would trigger repricing around taxes, regulation, financials, and the AI investment ecosystem; JPM year-end SPX target is 8,000.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning: Mag7 net bought +3z; AI exposure most sold this week; biotech de-grossing extreme
bullets.body: JPM Prime notes Mag7 was the most net bought theme globally at +3 standard deviations over the past 20 days, mostly via longs. However, UBS flags AI exposure (UBXXA100) was the most sold segment this week as funds take profits ahead of earnings. Biotech is experiencing the strongest 60-day de-grossing since early 2020; Utilities hedge fund net exposure hit new historical lows as rates rose.

bullets.title: AI bubble concentrated in private markets (OpenAI, Anthropic), not public large caps
bullets.body: Multiple sources converge on the view that AI valuation excess is in private markets — OpenAI and Anthropic burning billions with uncertain profitability paths — while public large-cap AI names (NVDA, META, MSFT) remain attractive on growth-adjusted multiples. Anthropic is targeting a $2T IPO before Thanksgiving with an investor day on Oct 14 and pre-IPO marketing beginning the week of Nov 9.

bullets.title: AVGO assembling $60B to fund Anthropic AI chip leases; AMZN offloading $8B NVDA chips via SPV
bullets.body: Broadcom is assembling ~$60B in financing ($42B senior-secured, $18B junior led by Blackstone) to fund AI chips for Anthropic and other frontier labs. Separately, Amazon is seeking to offload ~$8B of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips to investors via a new SPV to strengthen its balance sheet. NVDA and SoftBank also completed their combined $20B final investment in OpenAI's last private round.

bullets.title: Accenture +16% on Q4 beat: AI bookings 3x, revenue per employee +6%, FY27 guidance above consensus
bullets.body: ACN reported Q4 revenue of $18.68B (beat vs $17.75-18.4B guidance), EPS $3.29 vs $3.18 estimate, with bookings of $22B including 37 deals above $100M. AI-related revenue doubled y/y with 400+ new client engagements in FY26; FY27 guidance of 3-6% local currency revenue growth was above consensus. Valuation at 14.4x NTM P/E remains well below the 5-year average of 23x.

bullets.title: Toshiba doubling HDD production in FY27 with $380M Philippines investment; STX -11%, WDC -8%
bullets.body: Toshiba plans to double data-center HDD production by FY27, spending ¥60B ($380M) to expand its Philippines factory — the first significant HDD capex in nearly five years — targeting 30% market share (vs ~10% now). Seagate fell ~11% and Western Digital ~8% in pre-market on the supply expansion news.

bullets.title: Optical stocks rally 7-11% on reports of US restrictions on Chinese transceivers at 3.2T and above
bullets.body: COHR +11%, LITE +7.7%, CIEN +7.7% in pre-market on reports of U.S. export restrictions targeting Chinese optical transceivers at 3.2T speeds and above. The China component block narrative is reinforcing the bullish demand thesis for Western optical suppliers already benefiting from the AI infrastructure buildout.

bullets.title: EU DMA gatekeeper designation for Azure and AWS expected by November; fines up to 10% of global revenue
bullets.body: EU regulators are finalizing a determination that Microsoft Azure and Amazon AWS meet the DMA gatekeeper threshold, with a decision expected as early as November 2026 following a June preliminary ruling. If confirmed, both companies would have six months to achieve full compliance; repeated infringement could trigger fines of up to 20% of worldwide turnover or forced business sales.

bullets.title: FHFA bi-merge push threatens ~7-8% EPS at EFX and TRU; FICO pricing advantage at risk from VantageScore
bullets.body: FHFA Director Pulte is pushing to shift from tri-merge to bi-merge credit reporting, which would eliminate ~$85-90M revenue at TRU (~8% of 2026E EPS) and ~$100M at EFX (~7% of 2026E EPS). Simultaneously, FHFA is moving to a single LLPA grid for FICO and VantageScore, ending FICO's mortgage pricing premium; Rocket Mortgage has already designated VantageScore 4.0 as its preferred model.

bullets.title: Asia hedge funds net sold equities for 4 consecutive months; China positioning at 10th percentile
bullets.body: GS Prime Asia data shows Asian fundamental L/S managers up 1.4% in September (YTD +23.4%) but net selling accelerated, with short sales exceeding longs 2.4-to-1. China allocations fell to 7.2% net (10th percentile on 1-year basis); Korea saw the most aggressive selling with longs exceeding shorts 5-to-1 as net allocation fell to 4.4%. Taiwan was a modest outlier with marginal net buying.

bullets.title: Brazil first-round election Sunday; closest race ever with significant market repricing potential
bullets.body: Brazil's October 4 first-round election is described by multiple sources as the closest ever. BofA recommends short EUR/BRL ahead of the vote on cheap valuation, high carry, and a potentially market-positive outcome, while also recommending long NTN-F 2037 local bonds. September IPCA is expected to accelerate; JPM is hosting a Monday morning webinar on election market implications.

bullets.title: Memory cycle extending: Micron guides tighter supply/demand through 2027-28; HBM pricing rising
bullets.body: Micron's Q1 guide-higher confirmed DRAM pricing up high-teens q/q and NAND up ~30%, with supply/demand expected to tighten further through CY27-28. SK Hynix/Samsung DRAM exports hit an all-time high of $33B in September (+552% y/y). Micron flagged RAM shortages tightening through 2028; memory inflation poses direct cost risk across industrials and consumer electronics.

bullets.title: Q3 earnings setup strong: 28.9% EPS growth expected, second-best margin quarter ever; Tech as core long
bullets.body: JPM models 26Q3 at 28.9% EPS growth and 15.0% margins — would be the second-best margin quarter on record. Semis and Mag7 are expected to outperform; AI theme expected to persist. Banks are also favored given growth reboot and steeper curve potential, while rate-sensitives (Real Estate, Telecom, Utilities) are expected to lag.
